decision.summary: The Federal Reserve decided to keep its target interest rate at 0 to 1/4 percent.

changes.quote: Information received since the Federal Open Market Committee met in June indicates that economic growth so far this year has been considerably slower than the Committee had expected.
changes.explanation: The Fed acknowledges that the economy grew much slower this year than previously anticipated.

changes.quote: Indicators suggest a deterioration in overall labor market conditions in recent months, and the unemployment rate has moved up.
changes.explanation: Job market conditions worsened recently and unemployment increased.

changes.quote: Household spending has flattened out, investment in nonresidential structures is still weak, and the housing sector remains depressed.
changes.explanation: Consumer spending stopped growing, business structures remain weak, and housing is depressed.

changes.quote: Temporary factors, including the damping effect of higher food and energy prices on consumer purchasing power and spending as well as supply chain disruptions associated with the tragic events in Japan, appear to account for only some of the recent weakness in economic activity.
changes.explanation: Special factors like high commodity prices and supply disruptions only explain part of the economic weakness.

changes.quote: More recently, inflation has moderated as prices of energy and some commodities have declined from their earlier peaks.
changes.explanation: Inflation cooled down lately because energy and commodity prices dropped from prior highs.

tone_quotes.quote: The Committee now expects a somewhat slower pace of recovery over coming quarters than it did at the time of the previous meeting and anticipates that the unemployment rate will decline only gradually toward levels that the Committee judges to be consistent with its dual mandate.
Moreover, downside risks to the economic outlook have increased.

The Committee currently anticipates that economic conditions--including low rates of resource utilization and a subdued outlook for inflation over the medium run--are likely to warrant exceptionally low levels for the federal funds rate at least through mid-2013.

for_you.text: Card rates should not move on this decision; a $5,000 balance at about 12.89% APR costs about $53.71 a month in interest.

Mortgages track the 10-year Treasury yield, not the fed funds rate. The 10-year was 2.2% and moved -20 bp on the day; if that move passed through, the payment on a new $300,000 30-year loan at 4.55% would fall by about $35.55 a month.
Savings yields should stay roughly where they are, since the Fed held rates.
Unemployment was 9%, and employers added an average of 132k jobs a month over the prior 3 months.

for_country.text: CPI inflation was 3.6% over the past year (July 2011); core PCE inflation, the Fed's preferred gauge, was 1.7%, against a 2% goal.
Real GDP grew at a 2.7% annualized pace in the latest reported quarter.
The 2-year Treasury yield, the most Fed-sensitive market rate, moved -8 bp on the day.
The broad trade-weighted dollar moved 0.23% on the day.

whats_next: The statement signals that the Fed plans to keep rates exceptionally low at least through mid-2013 to support the recovery. According to educational forecast models, upcoming meetings have a 60% chance of a hold, 38% chance of a cut, and 2% chance of a hike.

citations.detail: the Committee decided today to keep the target range for the federal funds rate at 0 to 1/4 percent.
